g1.label: 1. today I ___ my family
g1.why: "today" contrasts with "usually" — it is a temporary activity, so use the present continuous.

g2.label: 2. My grandmother ___ soup right now
g2.why: "right now" shows an action in progress at this moment — use the present continuous.

g3.label: 3. She ___ soup every Saturday
g3.why: "every Saturday" is a regular habit — use the present simple, with -s for "she".

g4.label: 4. the whole family ___ to her house
g4.why: A repeated weekly event takes the present simple. "Family" is singular, so add -s.

g5.label: 5. My brother never ___ in the kitchen
g5.why: "never" is a frequency word, so use the present simple. "He" needs -s.

g6.label: 6. Right now he ___ football
g6.why: "Right now" means this moment — use am/is/are + -ing.

g1.label: 1. My sister ___ in a hospital
g1.why: A fact about her job: present simple. With "she", the verb ends in -s.

g2.label: 2. They ___ TV in the morning
g2.why: Negative with "they": don't + base verb. The verb after don't has no -s.

g3.label: 3. ___ you like pizza?
g3.why: Questions with "you" use Do + subject + base verb. "Are" is only for be.

g4.label: 4. Tom ___ to school by bike
g4.why: Daily habit with "he": the verb takes -es after go.

g5.label: 5. ___ she speak French?
g5.why: Questions with "she" use Does + base verb. After Does, "speak" has no -s.

g6.label: 6. Water ___ at 100 degrees
g6.why: A scientific fact is always present simple. "Water" is it, so add -s.

g7.label: 7. It ___ much in Cairo
g7.why: Negative with "it": doesn't + base verb. Never "doesn't rains".

g8.label: 8. My uncle is ___ engineer
g8.why: Spaced recall from esl-articles: a job takes "a/an", and "an" goes before the vowel sound in "engineer".

g9.label: 9. My parents ___ coffee in the evening
g9.why: Frequency words like "never" go before the main verb. "Parents" is plural, so no -s.

g1.label: 1. The baby ___
g1.why: "Be quiet!" tells you it is happening now — use the present continuous.

g2.label: 2. I ___ cereal every day
g2.why: "every day" signals a habit — use the present simple. "I" takes no -s.

g3.label: 3. Look! It ___ outside
g3.why: "Look!" points to something happening now — use the present continuous.

g4.label: 4. She ___ the answer
g4.why: "Know" is a state verb. We do not use state verbs in the continuous, even right now.

g5.label: 5. We ___ dinner at the moment
g5.why: Here "have" means eating, an action, and "at the moment" shows it is in progress — use the continuous.

g6.label: 6. He usually ___ jeans
g6.why: "usually" signals a habit — present simple, with -s for "he".

g7.label: 6. today he ___ a suit
g7.why: "today" contrasts with "usually" — a temporary situation, so use the present continuous.

g8.label: 7. I ___ this song
g8.why: "Love" is a state verb (a feeling), so use the present simple: "I love", not "I am loving".
